Stays of 30 days or fewer need an STR licence, except renting a room while the host stays home. Homestead unit: licence, max 10 occupants, licence ID on listing. Non-homestead: one licence per person, management and floor plan. Buildings over 20 units: max 10% STR (not condos). Code Title 12 Ch. 244.

records.summary: Since Dec 2017, stays under 30 days need yearly host and platform licences (Leg. Code Ch. 379). No commercial or social events. Units allowed per building depend on owner-occupancy (e.g. 1 in a non-owner-occupied duplex). Non-owner-occupied units need a Fire Certificate of Occupancy. Occupancy follows zoning and building code.

records.summary: June 2023 ordinances banned STRs in single-family zones and created registration. A court blocked enforcement (Dec 2023 injunction, largely upheld July 2025). Texas Supreme Court granted review Oct 23 2026, argument Dec 3 2026 (No. 25-0748). Rules in flux; hotel occupancy tax still applies.

records.summary: Stays under 30 days need a 2-year operating licence (Ch. 4-23). Since Feb 2025, STRs are an accessory use in all residential zones. Limits: 2 units per single-family site, others 1,000 ft apart; greater of 1 unit or 10% (multifamily) / 25% (mixed-use). Platforms must show licence field (July 2026). HOT applies.
records.cap: 2 per SF site; 1,000 ft spacing; 10% MF; 25% mixed-use
records.max_occupancy: 2 adults per bedroom + 2, 10pm-7am (LDC 25-2-795; confirm current text)

records.summary: Stays of 1-29 days need an STR licence, and the unit must be the host's primary residence: usual place of return, only one allowed, tax filings alone are not proof. Tenants need owner permission. Rentals of 30+ days need a residential rental licence instead. Lodger's tax applies.
records.display_number: required by DRMC (not confirmed on page)

records.summary: Stays of 29 days or fewer need a 4-year rental licence and are allowed only in the owner's principal residence, proven with a Colorado ID. Annual affidavit required. Not allowed on properties with an ADU (10-3-19). An accessory unit may be rented up to 120 days a year. Accommodations tax applies.

Rentals under 30 nights need an STR permit from the Building and Zoning Services License Section (City Code Ch. 598; ordinance 1959-2021). Applicants need a BCI background check. Check zoning first. Caps and occupancy in Ch. 598 not read.

Since July 1 2019, STRs must register before operating (Municipal Code Ch. 856). Registration lasts 3 years. Registration ID must appear in all listings; permit and advisory posted in the unit. 7% excise tax on gross revenue (Ch. 315); Airbnb remits under an agreement.

Stays under 30 days need an STR licence before advertising (Title 21 Ch. 26). Licence number must be on all ads and posted near the entry. Max 8 occupants regardless of size, and Title 55 s.404 may lower that. Events banned. 5% lodging tax monthly (5+ rooms). Fines up to $1,200 per violation.
records.cap: none; allowed in all zoning districts
records.max_occupancy: 8 total; plus Title 55 s.404 floor-area limits
records.penalties: misdemeanor up to $1,200/violation; civil up to $1,000/day; revocation after 3 violations in 12 months

records.summary: All STRs register (Ch. 56 Art. VIII). Resident STR: host lives there 270+ days a year; allowed in residential zones. Non-resident STRs banned in residential zones unless grandfathered; 1,000 ft spacing for 1-2 unit buildings; max 12.5% of units in 3+ unit buildings. Number on listings. 7.5% transient tax.
records.primary_residence: resident type only, in residential zones

records.summary: Stays of 179 days or less need a business licence after zoning approval. STRs are zoned like motels, so most residential zones bar them. Allowed as a primary use in Residence 2-B, C-3, C-4, C-5, industrial, research park and airport districts. 9% lodging tax plus $2 per room-night via Alabama ONE SPOT.
records.ordinance: City Code Ch. 15 Arts. II-III (tax); Zoning Ordinance

No statute bars local STR rules, but Zaatari v. City of Austin (2019) struck Austin's non-owner-occupied ban, and Dallas's zoning ban is before the Texas Supreme Court. Rent control is preempted (Local Gov't Code 214.902), as are local voucher/source-of-income mandates (250.007).

No enacted STR preemption (bills such as HB 563 of 2022 failed). Home-rule cities may license STRs. R.C. Chapter 5323 requires residential rental owners to register with the county auditor. Local rent control: no enabling law; treated as unavailable (unsettled).

No statewide STR preemption enacted (bills filed repeatedly). Rent control preempted by RSMo 441.043. Kansas City's resident/non-resident rules apply.

records.summary: IPMC s.404: bedrooms need at least 70 sq ft for one occupant and 50 sq ft per occupant beyond that. Habitable rooms need a 7 ft minimum dimension. Sleeping rooms need emergency egress (s.702.4, tied to the building code). Cities amend when adopting: check the local version.

IRC R310: each sleeping room needs an emergency escape opening of at least 5.7 sq ft net clear (5.0 at grade), 24 in high, 20 in wide, with the sill no higher than 44 in. R304: habitable rooms at least 70 sq ft and 7 ft in any direction.

Federal bunk-bed safety standard 16 CFR 1513 (guardrails, opening sizes); CPSC advises no child under 6 on the top bunk. None of the target-city STR ordinances reviewed had bunk-bed rules (Tulsa caps total occupants; Austin caps adults per bedroom).
